questions.q: What is a noun?
options: A naming word — a person, place, or thing
questions.answer: A naming word — a person, place, or thing
questions.explain: A noun names a person, place, thing, or idea.
procedure: A noun is a naming word
Answer: A naming word — a person, place, or thing

questions.q: Which of these is a noun?
questions.explain: 'Teacher' is a noun — it names a person.
procedure: Nouns name people, places, or things

questions.q: What is a verb?
options: An action word or state of being
questions.answer: An action word or state of being
questions.explain: A verb shows action or state of being.
procedure: They show what someone or something does
Verbs also show states of being (is, are, was)
Answer: An action word or state of being

questions.q: Which of these is a verb?
questions.explain: 'Dance' is a verb — it shows an action.

questions.q: What is an adjective?
options: A word that describes a noun
A word that describes a verb
questions.answer: A word that describes a noun
questions.explain: Adjectives describe or add meaning to nouns.
procedure: They tell us what kind, how many, or which one
Answer: A word that describes a noun

questions.q: Which word is an adjective in this sentence: 'The tall boy ran quickly.'
questions.explain: 'Tall' describes the noun 'boy' — so it's an adjective.
procedure: What kind of boy? A 'tall' boy

questions.q: What is an adverb?
options: A word that describes a noun
A word that describes a verb, adjective, or another adverb
questions.answer: A word that describes a verb, adjective, or another adverb
questions.explain: Adverbs describe how, when, or where an action happens.
procedure: Adverbs describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs
They can answer: how? when? where?
Answer: A word that describes a verb, adjective, or another adverb

questions.q: Which word is an adverb in this sentence: 'She sang beautifully.'
questions.explain: 'Beautifully' describes how she sang — so it's an adverb.
procedure: Adverbs tell us HOW something happened

questions.q: What is a pronoun?
options: A word that replaces a noun
questions.answer: A word that replaces a noun
questions.explain: Pronouns replace nouns — like he, she, it, they, we.
procedure: A pronoun stands in place of a noun
Instead of saying 'Kofi ran', we say 'He ran'
Examples: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
Answer: A word that replaces a noun

questions.q: Which of these is a pronoun?
questions.explain: 'She' is a pronoun — it replaces a female person's name.

questions.q: What is a preposition?
options: A word that shows the position or relationship between things
questions.answer: A word that shows the position or relationship between things
questions.explain: Prepositions show relationships — in, on, under, beside, between.
procedure: Examples: in, on, under, beside, between
The cat is UNDER the table
Answer: A word that shows the position or relationship between things

questions.q: Which of these is a preposition?
questions.explain: 'Under' is a preposition — it shows position.

questions.q: What is a conjunction?
questions.explain: Conjunctions join words, phrases, or sentences — and, but, or, because.
procedure: Examples: and, but, or, because, so

questions.q: Which of these is a conjunction?
questions.explain: 'And' joins two ideas together — it's a conjunction.

questions.q: Which word is a noun in the sentence: 'The red car is fast.'
questions.explain: 'Car' is a noun — it names a thing.

questions.q: What is the noun in: 'They live in Kumasi.'
questions.explain: 'Kumasi' is a noun — it names a place.
procedure: Nouns name people, places, or things

questions.q: Which of these sentences uses an adjective?
questions.explain: 'Big' describes 'dog' — so it's an adjective.
procedure: Answer: The big dog barks loudly.

questions.q: Identify the verb in: 'The children play football.'
questions.explain: 'Play' is a verb — it's the action the children do.
procedure: What are the children doing? Playing

questions.q: Identify the adverb in: 'They arrived late.'
questions.explain: 'Late' describes when they arrived — so it's an adverb.
procedure: Adverbs tell us WHEN, HOW, or WHERE

questions.q: Which part of speech is the word 'quickly'?
questions.explain: 'Quickly' tells us HOW something is done — it's an adverb.
procedure: It describes how something is done

questions.q: Which part of speech is the word 'happy'?
questions.explain: 'Happy' is an adjective — it describes a noun (a happy person).
procedure: A 'happy' person = happy describes the person

questions.q: What is the present tense?
options: It shows actions in the past
It shows actions in the future
It shows actions that never happen
questions.explain: The present tense describes actions happening now.
procedure: The action is happening in the present
Answer: It shows actions happening now

questions.q: What is the past tense?
options: It shows actions that already happened
questions.answer: It shows actions that already happened
questions.explain: The past tense describes actions that already happened.
procedure: Answer: It shows actions that already happened

questions.q: What is the future tense?
options: It shows actions that have not yet happened
questions.answer: It shows actions that have not yet happened
questions.explain: The future tense describes actions that will happen.
procedure: Answer: It shows actions that have not yet happened

questions.q: Choose the correct past tense: 'Yesterday, I ____ to school.'

questions.q: Choose the correct future tense: 'Tomorrow, she ____ her grandmother.'
questions.explain: 'Will visit' is the future tense.

questions.q: Which sentence is in the present tense?
questions.explain: 'Walk' is present tense — the action happens now.
procedure: Present tense uses the base verb

questions.q: What is the present continuous tense?
options: It shows an action happening right now
It shows an action in the past
It shows an action in the future
It shows an action that never happened
questions.answer: It shows an action happening right now
questions.explain: Present continuous shows actions happening right now — I am walking.
procedure: The action is happening RIGHT NOW
Answer: It shows an action happening right now

questions.q: Choose the correct present continuous: 'Look! The baby ____.'
questions.explain: 'Is crying' is present continuous.

questions.q: Which is the past tense of 'eat'?

questions.q: Which is the past tense of 'run'?
questions.explain: 'Ran' is the correct past tense of 'run'.

questions.q: Which of these is a future tense sentence?
questions.explain: 'Will eat' shows a future action.

questions.q: Which is correct: 'She ____ her homework already.'
questions.explain: 'Already' suggests the action is complete — past tense.

questions.q: What is the correct present continuous of 'sleep' in: 'The cat ____ on the sofa.'
questions.explain: The cat is sleeping — present continuous.

questions.q: Which is the past continuous tense?
questions.explain: Past continuous uses 'was/were + verb-ing'.

questions.explain: 'By next year' means the future — so 'will be' is correct.

questions.answer: She goes to school every day.

questions.q: Which is the correct past tense: 'They ____ football yesterday.'
questions.explain: 'Yesterday' needs past tense — 'played'.

questions.q: What does 'has eaten' show?

questions.answer: Present perfect — action completed before now

Answer: Present perfect — action completed before now

questions.q: Which is correct: 'I ____ to Accra next week.'

questions.explain: 'Flew' is the past tense of 'fly'.
procedure: 'Opened' is past, so 'fly' should also be past

questions.q: What is a synonym?
options: A word with the opposite meaning
A word with the same or similar meaning
A word borrowed from another language
questions.answer: A word with the same or similar meaning
questions.explain: Synonyms are words with similar meanings.
procedure: Answer: A word with the same or similar meaning

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'happy'?
questions.explain: 'Glad' is a synonym for 'happy'.
procedure: Happy and glad both mean joyful

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'big'?
questions.explain: 'Huge' is a synonym for 'big'.
procedure: Big and huge both mean large

questions.q: What is an antonym?
options: A word with the same meaning
A word with the opposite meaning
questions.answer: A word with the opposite meaning
questions.explain: Antonyms are words with opposite meanings.
procedure: Answer: A word with the opposite meaning

questions.q: Which is an antonym for 'hot'?
questions.explain: 'Cold' is the antonym of 'hot'.
procedure: The opposite of hot is cold

questions.q: Which is an antonym for 'brave'?
questions.explain: 'Cowardly' is the antonym of 'brave'.
procedure: Its opposite is cowardly = lacking courage

questions.q: What are homophones?
options: Words that sound the same but are spelled differently
Words with the same spelling but different meanings
questions.answer: Words that sound the same but are spelled differently
questions.explain: Homophones sound the same but have different spellings and meanings.
procedure: Answer: Words that sound the same but are spelled differently

questions.q: Which pair are homophones?
questions.explain: 'There' and 'their' sound the same — they're homophones.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym for 'quick'?
questions.explain: 'Fast' is a synonym for 'quick'.
procedure: Quick and fast mean the same thing

questions.q: Which word is an antonym for 'strong'?
questions.explain: 'Weak' is the opposite of 'strong'.

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'ancient'?
questions.explain: 'Ancient' means very old — from a long time ago.

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'enormous'?
questions.explain: 'Enormous' means very large or huge.

questions.q: What does 'brave' mean?
options: Ready to face danger without fear
questions.answer: Ready to face danger without fear
questions.explain: 'Brave' means having courage to face danger.
procedure: Answer: Ready to face danger without fear

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'gather'?
questions.explain: 'Gather' means to bring things or people together.

questions.q: Which word means 'to look at something carefully'?
questions.explain: 'Examine' means to look at something carefully.

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'difficult'?
questions.explain: 'Difficult' means hard — not easy.
procedure: Answer: Not easy — hard to do

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'furious'?
questions.explain: 'Furious' means extremely angry.

questions.q: What does 'curious' mean?
options: Wanting to know or learn something
questions.answer: Wanting to know or learn something
questions.explain: 'Curious' means wanting to know or learn more.
procedure: Answer: Wanting to know or learn something

questions.q: Which word means 'to say sorry'?
questions.explain: 'Apologize' means to say sorry.

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'immediately'?
questions.explain: 'Immediately' means right now, without delay.

questions.q: What does a full stop (.) show?
options: That a question is being asked
questions.explain: A full stop marks the end of a sentence.
procedure: A full stop is a small dot (.)
It marks the end of a statement
Answer: That a sentence has ended

questions.q: Which sentence needs a full stop?
questions.explain: All three need punctuation.
procedure: Every sentence needs an end punctuation

questions.q: What does a question mark (?) show?
options: That a question is being asked
questions.answer: That a question is being asked
questions.explain: A question mark shows that a question is being asked.
procedure: It goes at the end of a question
Answer: That a question is being asked

questions.q: Which sentence needs a question mark?
questions.explain: 'Where are you going' is a question.

questions.q: What does an exclamation mark (!) show?
options: That a sentence is a statement
That a sentence is a question
Strong emotion — surprise, excitement, or a command
questions.answer: Strong emotion — surprise, excitement, or a command
questions.explain: An exclamation mark shows strong emotion or a command.
procedure: Answer: Strong emotion — surprise, excitement, or a command

questions.q: Which sentence needs an exclamation mark?
questions.explain: 'Wow that is amazing' shows surprise.

questions.q: What does a comma (,) do?
options: Shows the end of a sentence
Separates items in a list or pauses a sentence
questions.answer: Separates items in a list or pauses a sentence
questions.explain: A comma separates items in a list or creates a small pause.
procedure: Answer: Separates items in a list or pauses a sentence

questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
options: I like red blue and green.
I like red, blue, and green.
I like red, blue and, green.
questions.answer: I like red, blue, and green.
questions.explain: Commas separate list items.
procedure: Answer: I like red, blue, and green.

questions.q: What does an apostrophe (') show?
options: That something is missing or belongs to someone
That someone is asking a question
questions.answer: That something is missing or belongs to someone
questions.explain: Apostrophes show possession or missing letters.
procedure: Answer: That something is missing or belongs to someone

questions.q: Which is correct?

procedure: For possession, add 's after the noun

questions.q: What does 'don't' stand for?
questions.explain: 'Don't' is a contraction of 'do not'.

questions.q: Which sentence has correct punctuation?

questions.q: What does a colon (:) do?

Answer: Shows a pause before a list or explanation

questions.q: What does a semicolon (;) do?

questions.q: What does a hyphen (-) do?

questions.q: What does 'Where there's a will, there's a way' mean?
options: If you really want something, you'll find a way to achieve it
questions.answer: If you really want something, you'll find a way to achieve it
questions.explain: Determination leads to solutions.
procedure: Answer: If you really want something, you'll find a way to achieve it

questions.q: What is a paragraph?
options: A group of sentences about one topic
questions.answer: A group of sentences about one topic
questions.explain: A paragraph is a group of sentences about one idea.
procedure: A paragraph is more than one sentence
All sentences relate to the same topic
Answer: A group of sentences about one topic

questions.q: What is a topic sentence?
options: The sentence that tells the main idea of a paragraph
questions.answer: The sentence that tells the main idea of a paragraph
questions.explain: A topic sentence states the main idea.
procedure: It tells what the paragraph is about
Answer: The sentence that tells the main idea of a paragraph

questions.q: What should every composition have?
questions.explain: A good composition has a clear structure.
procedure: Answer: A beginning, middle, and end

questions.q: What is an introduction?
options: The beginning — it introduces the topic
questions.answer: The beginning — it introduces the topic
questions.explain: The introduction is the opening of a composition.
procedure: It's the start of a composition
Answer: The beginning — it introduces the topic

questions.q: What is a conclusion?
options: The ending — it wraps up the composition
questions.answer: The ending — it wraps up the composition
questions.explain: The conclusion summarises the main points.
procedure: Answer: The ending — it wraps up the composition

questions.q: What is an informal letter?
options: A letter to a friend or family member
A letter to a school principal
questions.answer: A letter to a friend or family member
questions.explain: Informal letters are casual.
procedure: Answer: A letter to a friend or family member

questions.q: What is a formal letter?
options: A letter to a company, official, or organisation
questions.answer: A letter to a company, official, or organisation
questions.explain: Formal letters are official.
procedure: Answer: A letter to a company, official, or organisation

questions.q: How should an informal letter end?
questions.explain: Informal letters end with casual phrases.

questions.q: How should a formal letter end?
questions.explain: Formal letters end with 'Yours faithfully' or 'Yours sincerely'.

questions.q: What is a narrative composition?
options: A story — describing events that happened
questions.answer: A story — describing events that happened
questions.explain: A narrative composition tells a story.
procedure: Answer: A story — describing events that happened

questions.q: What is a descriptive composition?
options: A composition that describes something in detail
questions.answer: A composition that describes something in detail
questions.explain: A descriptive composition paints a picture with words.
procedure: Answer: A composition that describes something in detail

questions.q: What is an argumentative composition?
options: A composition that argues for or against an opinion
questions.answer: A composition that argues for or against an opinion
questions.explain: An argumentative composition presents a view.
procedure: Answer: A composition that argues for or against an opinion

questions.q: What does a good composition have at the start?
options: An interesting opening that hooks the reader
questions.answer: An interesting opening that hooks the reader
questions.explain: A good composition starts with an interesting opening.
procedure: Answer: An interesting opening that hooks the reader

questions.q: How many paragraphs should a short composition have?
questions.explain: Introduction, body, and conclusion.

questions.q: What should you do before writing a composition?
options: Ask a friend to write it
questions.explain: Planning helps organise your thoughts.

questions.q: What is a title?
questions.explain: A title is the name of a composition.
procedure: Answer: The name of a composition

questions.q: What should every sentence in a composition begin with?
questions.explain: Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a dialogue in a composition?
options: To show characters speaking to each other
questions.answer: To show characters speaking to each other
questions.explain: Dialogue shows characters speaking.
procedure: Answer: To show characters speaking to each other

questions.q: Which is the correct way to write dialogue?
questions.explain: Dialogue needs quotation marks.
procedure: Spoken words go in quotation marks

questions.q: Why should we read our composition after writing it?
questions.explain: Reading over your work helps catch errors.
procedure: Answer: To find and fix mistakes

questions.q: What is direct speech?
options: Reporting what someone said, using exact words
Reporting what someone said without exact words
questions.answer: Reporting what someone said, using exact words
questions.explain: Direct speech uses the exact words someone said, in quotation marks.
procedure: Direct speech uses the person's exact words
Answer: Reporting what someone said, using exact words

questions.q: What is indirect speech?
options: Reporting someone's words without the exact words
Using exact words in quotation marks
questions.answer: Reporting someone's words without the exact words
questions.explain: Indirect speech reports what someone said without using quotation marks.
procedure: Indirect speech reports the meaning, not the exact words
Example: She said (that) she was happy.
Answer: Reporting someone's words without the exact words

questions.q: Which sentence is in direct speech?
options: She said that she was tired.
questions.explain: Direct speech uses quotation marks and exact words.
procedure: "I am tired." is the exact speech

questions.q: Which sentence is in indirect speech?
options: He said that he would come.
questions.answer: He said that he would come.
questions.explain: Indirect speech reports the words without quotation marks.
procedure: Indirect speech doesn't use quotation marks
Answer: He said that he would come.

questions.q: What happens to the pronoun in: 'She said, "I am happy."' when changed to indirect speech?
questions.explain: In indirect speech, 'I' becomes 'she' because we are reporting what she said.
procedure: In indirect speech: She said that SHE was happy.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'Kofi said, "I am going home."'
options: Kofi said that he is going home.
Kofi said that he was going home.
Kofi said that I am going home.
Kofi said that he will go home.
questions.answer: Kofi said that he was going home.
questions.explain: Present continuous 'am going' becomes past continuous 'was going' in indirect speech.
procedure: Reported speech shifts one step back in tense
Answer: Kofi said that he was going home.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'Ama said, "I will eat rice."'
options: Ama said that she will eat rice.
Ama said that she would eat rice.
Ama said that I will eat rice.
Ama said that I would eat rice.
questions.answer: Ama said that she would eat rice.
questions.explain: 'Will' becomes 'would' in indirect speech.
procedure: Answer: Ama said that she would eat rice.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'The teacher said, "Open your books."'
options: The teacher said to open your books.
The teacher said that open your books.
The teacher said to open our books.
The teacher said opened your books.
questions.answer: The teacher said to open our books.
questions.explain: For commands, 'said' becomes 'told' or 'asked', and 'your' becomes 'our'.
procedure: Answer: The teacher said to open our books.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'Mother asked, "Are you hungry?"'
options: Mother asked if I was hungry.
Mother asked am I am hungry.
questions.answer: Mother asked if I was hungry.
questions.explain: For yes/no questions, use 'if' or 'whether'.
procedure: Answer: Mother asked if I was hungry.

questions.q: What happens to quotation marks in indirect speech?
questions.explain: Indirect speech does not use quotation marks.

questions.q: Which pronoun change is correct: 'He said, "I am tired."'
questions.explain: When reporting 'he said', 'I' becomes 'he'.
procedure: Indirect: He said (that) HE was tired.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'They said, "We are playing."'
questions.explain: 'We' becomes 'they', and 'are playing' becomes 'were playing'.
procedure: Answer: They said they were playing.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'She said, "I have finished."'
questions.explain: Present perfect 'have finished' becomes past perfect 'had finished'.
procedure: Answer: She said she had finished.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'He said, "I came yesterday."'
options: He said he had come the day before.
He said he will come yesterday.
questions.answer: He said he had come the day before.
questions.explain: Past tense becomes past perfect, and 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.
procedure: Answer: He said he had come the day before.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'The boy said, "I can swim."'
options: The boy said he can swim.
The boy said he could swim.
The boy said he will swim.
The boy said he is swimming.
questions.answer: The boy said he could swim.
questions.explain: 'Can' becomes 'could' in indirect speech.
procedure: Answer: The boy said he could swim.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'She said, "I may come."'
questions.explain: 'May' becomes 'might' in indirect speech.
procedure: Answer: She said she might come.

questions.q: Change to indirect speech: 'Kofi said, "I must go."'
options: Kofi said he had to go.
questions.answer: Kofi said he had to go.
questions.explain: 'Must' becomes 'had to' in indirect speech.
procedure: Answer: Kofi said he had to go.

questions.q: What happens to 'today' in indirect speech?
questions.explain: 'Today' becomes 'that day' in indirect speech.
procedure: Time words change in indirect speech

questions.q: What happens to 'tomorrow' in indirect speech?
questions.explain: 'Tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' or 'the following day'.
procedure: Answer: It changes to 'the next day'

questions.q: What happens to 'here' in indirect speech?
questions.explain: 'Here' becomes 'there' in indirect speech.
procedure: Place words change in indirect speech

questions.q: What is active voice?
questions.explain: In active voice, the subject performs the action.
procedure: Active voice = subject does the action
Answer: The subject does the action

questions.q: What is passive voice?
questions.explain: In passive voice, the subject receives the action.
procedure: Passive voice = subject receives the action
Example: 'The ball was kicked by the boy'
Answer: The subject receives the action

questions.q: Which sentence is in active voice?
options: The ball was kicked by the boy.
questions.explain: The boy (subject) performs the action — active voice.
procedure: Answer: The boy kicked the ball.

questions.q: Which sentence is in passive voice?
options: The ball was kicked by the boy.
The boy is kicking the ball.
The boy will kick the ball.
questions.answer: The ball was kicked by the boy.
questions.explain: The ball receives the action — passive voice.
procedure: Answer: The ball was kicked by the boy.

questions.q: Change to passive: 'The dog chased the cat.'
options: The cat was chased by the dog.
The dog was chased by the cat.
The dog is chasing the cat.
questions.answer: The cat was chased by the dog.
questions.explain: The object (cat) becomes the subject, and 'was chased by the dog' is added.
procedure: Answer: The cat was chased by the dog.

questions.q: Change to active: 'The letter was written by Ama.'
questions.explain: The doer (Ama) becomes the subject.

questions.q: Change to passive: 'The children ate the mangoes.'
options: The mangoes were eaten by the children.
The children were eaten by the mangoes.
The children are eating the mangoes.
questions.answer: The mangoes were eaten by the children.
questions.explain: 'Ate' becomes 'were eaten', object becomes subject.
procedure: Answer: The mangoes were eaten by the children.

questions.q: Change to active: 'The cake was baked by mother.'
questions.explain: The doer (mother) becomes the subject.

questions.q: What happens to the verb in passive voice?
questions.explain: In passive voice, the verb uses a form of 'to be' + past participle.
procedure: Passive voice uses 'to be' + past participle
Answer: It becomes 'to be' + past participle

questions.q: What word is often used in passive voice to show who did the action?
questions.explain: In passive voice, 'by' introduces the doer.
procedure: 'The ball was kicked BY the boy'

questions.q: Change to passive: 'She sings a song.'
options: A song is sung by her.
She is sung by a song.
A song was sung by her.
questions.answer: A song is sung by her.
questions.explain: 'Sings' becomes 'is sung', 'she' becomes 'her'.
procedure: Answer: A song is sung by her.

questions.q: Change to active: 'The window was broken by the boys.'
options: The window is breaking the boys.
The boys were broken by the window.
questions.explain: The doer (the boys) becomes the subject.
procedure: Answer: The boys broke the window.

questions.q: Which sentence is NOT in passive voice?
options: The book was read by Kofi.
The food was cooked by mother.
questions.explain: The children are the subject, and they do the action — active voice.
procedure: 'The children play football' — children do the action

questions.q: Which sentence is in passive voice?
options: The students are taught by the teacher.
questions.answer: The students are taught by the teacher.
questions.explain: The students receive the action ('are taught').
procedure: 'The students are taught' — they receive teaching
Answer: The students are taught by the teacher.

questions.q: Change to passive: 'They will build a new school.'
options: A new school will be built by them.
A new school will build them.
They will be built by a new school.
A new school is built by them.
questions.answer: A new school will be built by them.
questions.explain: 'Will build' becomes 'will be built', 'they' becomes 'them'.
procedure: Answer: A new school will be built by them.

questions.q: Change to active: 'The song was sung by the girls.'
options: The girls are singing the song.
The song is sung by the girls.
questions.explain: The doer (the girls) becomes the subject.
procedure: Answer: The girls sang the song.

questions.q: Change to passive: 'The cat drinks milk.'
options: Milk is drunk by the cat.
The cat was drunk by milk.
Milk was drunk by the cat.
questions.answer: Milk is drunk by the cat.
questions.explain: Present tense passive: 'is drunk by the cat'.
procedure: Answer: Milk is drunk by the cat.

questions.q: Change to active: 'The tree was planted by the children.'
options: The tree is planting the children.
The children are planting the tree.
questions.explain: The doer (children) becomes the subject.
procedure: Answer: The children planted the tree.

questions.q: What is the passive form of 'Someone has stolen my bag'?
questions.explain: 'Has stolen' becomes 'has been stolen'.
procedure: Answer: My bag has been stolen.

questions.q: Change to passive: 'People speak English here.'
questions.explain: 'People speak' becomes 'is spoken' (no 'by' needed).
procedure: When the doer is unknown or general, drop 'by'
